summary:
Giresun province stands under the national framework of Türkiye. The source inventory contains no Giresun-specific finding on trans rights, so every assessment below describes national law and practice that applies inside the province.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked omnibus draft, the 11th Judicial Package, would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise LGBT conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' with up to 3 years' imprisonment, and would criminalise same-sex ceremonies with up to 4 years. The same package would raise the eligibility age for gender-affirming healthcare from 18 to 25, add mandatory infertility and repeated-evaluation conditions, and expose providers to fines and up to 7 years' imprisonment and patients to up to 3 years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected to the draft. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.

Homosexuality has been decriminalised since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988, with gender-reassignment surgery legal since 1988. Same-sex marriage, civil unions and joint adoption are not recognised, and LGBTQ people are barred from openly serving in the military. Turkey has no comprehensive national law banning discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity.

A court case to close Lambda Istanbul was overruled by the Constitutional Court, keeping the association open. Pride events have been banned in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants. ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking placed Turkey 47th out of 49 countries.
tangentialFactors:
The 11th Judicial Package sits within a broader authoritarian drift under the Erdoğan government, which has repeatedly used 'the family' and 'public morals' framing to legitimise stigmatisation of LGBT people.

The Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 records 313 violations over the year, roughly two and a half times the 2024 total, dominated by 299 detention decisions — 256 taken on the record and 43 off it — alongside systematic attacks on the privacy of LGBT people. Turkish Minute's coverage of the same report counts six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025, three classified as hate killings, with transgender individuals disproportionately affected.

ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking placed Turkey 47th out of 49 countries, a comparative position consistent with the documented enforcement pattern.

outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has since passed is unresolved in the sources; Human Rights Watch reported on the leaked draft as of 29 October 2025.

No usable Giresun-specific finding on trans rights is recorded in the source inventory, so the province-level picture rests entirely on national data.

The source inventory does not document local police or municipal practice in Giresun itself; enforcement accounts cited here come from Istanbul, Ankara and other provinces.
